incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: Attackers drained funds from the exchange across multiple wallets; the precise intrusion method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Up to $6.3 billion in funds was affected in what is being called the largest crypto heist on record; roughly $1.2-3 billion in USDT and ETH escaped recovery despite partial freezes by Tether and Circle.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense/intelligence agencies, and 19 U.S. pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial firms, plus telecoms in the U.S., Belgium and the Philippines
incidents.vector: Used the ARTEX agentic AI penetration-testing framework paired with the DeepSeek model to automate reconnaissance and exploitation at machine speed (up to 1,500 commands per hour) against 200+ organizations in 14 countries.
incidents.impact: About 140 of 200+ targeted organizations were compromised or showed evidence of intrusion within 11 days, including a European country's presidency and prime minister's office.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education (Florida Student Financial Aid website)
incidents.vector: An unauthorized party gained access to a system or database containing student financial-aid applicant information.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, phone numbers, genders, emails, Social Security numbers and dates of birth of nearly 5 million people were exposed; the site was taken offline.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian manufacturing company supporting the country's transportation sector
incidents.attacker: Belarus — state-linked, acting as a Russian proxy
incidents.vector: Deployed destructive wiper malware against the victim's network — Belarus's first publicly documented use of wiper malware.
incidents.impact: A data-wiping attack disrupted operations at a Ukrainian company supporting the country's transportation sector; researchers note Belarus-aligned groups are increasingly acting as cyber proxies for Russia.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (ICE and CBP employees)
incidents.vector: Breached an Okta single sign-on database used by DHS and exfiltrated employee personnel records dating back to 2011.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 41,000 DHS employees, mostly ICE and CBP staff, was published online by a hacktivist group calling itself "Department of Peace."

incidents.victim: GMO Internet Group (Onamae Desktop Cloud / FX trading platform)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to GMO's Onamae Desktop Cloud service hosting its foreign-exchange trading platform.
incidents.impact: Attackers demanded a $50 million ransom and leaked some stolen data on the dark web; GMO is offering a $1 million reward for information on the attackers.

incidents.victim: Multiple U.S. companies, including a defense-adjacent generative AI contractor
incidents.vector: A U.S. defense contractor with a security clearance let North Korean operatives use his identity to apply for remote IT jobs and hosted laptops shipped by victim companies to enable remote access.
incidents.impact: Scheme spanned 88 job applications and 9 job offers; one co-conspirator briefly gained access to a generative AI project for a U.S. military contract before discovery. Treasury separately sanctioned other facilitators of the broader DPRK IT-worker scheme on Oct. 28.

incidents.victim: U.S. Navy personnel and installations (Navy Base Kitsap, Navy recruiting stations)
incidents.vector: Two PRC nationals operated as MSS agents, facilitating clandestine cash "dead drop" payments and gathering photos and personal information on U.S. Navy personnel and installations to recruit intelligence assets.
incidents.impact: Liren Lai and Yuance Chen were sentenced to 30 months in prison each for acting as unregistered foreign agents on behalf of the PRC's Ministry of State Security.

incidents.victim: Revolve Group
incidents.vector: Threat actors used automated means to access company systems and obtain saved payment card numbers and expiration dates from the retailer's e-commerce platform.
incidents.impact: At least 127,200 Texas residents and additional victims in Vermont and Massachusetts were affected; the company does not expect material financial impact.

incidents.victim: Unidentified Asian government agency (customized Windows 10 build)
incidents.vector: Malware was bundled inside a package in the Windows update directory using legitimate signed Microsoft components and the third-party Patch My PC update tool, suggesting a software supply-chain compromise.
incidents.impact: Only one infected system has been confirmed; the malware, dubbed NetamLoader, can disable security scanning, delete logs and exfiltrate data, though no confirmed data theft has been established.

incidents.victim: Associated Press, U.S. Marine Corps recruitment site host, White House staff, and roughly 47 media, NGO and government entities
incidents.vector: Compromised the AP's Twitter account to post a false White House bombing claim, and separately hijacked a Marine Corps recruiting site host and stole White House staff credentials.
incidents.impact: The 2013 false tweet triggered a flash crash that briefly erased $136 billion in stock market value; a global NGO victim alone suffered $480,000 in losses. Ahmad Umar Agha was sentenced to 42 months in federal prison.

incidents.victim: Nomad Bridge (cryptocurrency bridge protocol)
incidents.vector: Exploited a flaw in the Nomad Bridge smart contract to execute unauthorized transactions, stealing wrapped Bitcoin and Ether.
incidents.impact: Approximately $2.89 million in cryptocurrency was stolen in 2022; Alexander Gurevich was extradited from Israel and made his first U.S. court appearance.

incidents.victim: Cursor IDE users (up to 5,000 affected)
incidents.vector: An attacker compromised the Cursor extension marketplace and swapped Anthropic's legitimate Claude Code extension for a malicious version containing a hidden loader that attempted to install an SSH backdoor and exfiltrate host reconnaissance data.
incidents.impact: The malicious version was live for about 11 hours; Cursor says at most 5,000 users were affected, with stolen data limited to hostnames, usernames, OS details and environment-variable names (not secret values). Anthropic's own systems were not compromised.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks customers with internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces (~0.02% of installed base)
incidents.vector: Chained the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618/109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw to gain root access to internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: A small fraction of Palo Alto Networks customers with internet-facing management interfaces were affected; the vendor individually contacted each one, and patched customers are protected.

incidents.victim: Polymarket and its customers
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised third-party web-performance provider DebugBear and injected wallet-draining JavaScript via its embed code on Polymarket's site.
incidents.impact: Trading was temporarily halted and more than $2.1 million in cryptocurrency was drained from user wallets; Polymarket says affected users will be fully reimbursed.

incidents.victim: U.S. Federal Election Commission
incidents.vector: An intrusion into FEC systems was detected, prompting the agency to shut down its electronic campaign-finance filing system.
incidents.impact: The filing system was taken offline a week before the U.S. Midterm elections; the FEC says there is no impact to the voting process itself.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited and downstream TLS certificate holders
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra emSign G3 intermediate certificate authority private keys were generated with insufficient cryptographic randomness, allowing the keys to potentially be derived from their public certificates.
incidents.impact: The weak keys could be used to forge trusted TLS certificates and conduct traffic interception; major browser and OS vendors revoked trust in the affected intermediates.

incidents.victim: Poryadok (Russian home-goods retail chain, 48 stores)
incidents.vector: Unspecified cyberattack on company IT systems; the retailer has not disclosed how hackers breached its network.
incidents.impact: Website, mobile app and in-store services were unavailable for five consecutive days; customers were unable to collect orders or access loyalty accounts.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government IT networks and began exfiltrating data before being detected by government IT staff.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly one-third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise customers (2,250+ downstream Microsoft 365 tenants) across manufacturing, aerospace, chemicals, energy, defense and financial services
incidents.vector: Compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application credentials, then used the ARTEX agentic AI pentesting framework to automate password spraying and OAuth abuse against thousands of tenants (up to 2,900 sign-in attempts per minute).
incidents.impact: Attackers obtained privileged cloud access at multiple organizations within hours; ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security and Cloud Management services.

incidents.victim: Approximately 600 organizations across the Americas, Europe and Australia
incidents.vector: Gains access via compromised credentials and known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN devices, then disables backups before stealing data and encrypting systems.
incidents.impact: One of the most active ransomware groups of 2026, with roughly 600 confirmed victims; CISA, FBI and the U.S. Secret Service issued a joint advisory with mitigations.

incidents.victim: John Deere, SharkNinja, a Cummins third-party vendor, and roughly 100 e-commerce/payment sites globally
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — payment card and cryptocurrency theft
incidents.vector: Used the AI-driven penetration-testing tool Cairn to automate discovery of SQL injection, insecure file upload and authentication-bypass flaws, then deployed web shells for persistent access to e-commerce sites.
incidents.impact: Researchers found over 1,100 attack projects across 14 exposed dashboards; John Deere and SharkNinja say the incidents were contained with no confirmed major data loss, while Cummins was still investigating a third-party vendor's site.

incidents.victim: Nearly 100 organizations, including the FBI and medical device maker Intuitive Surgical
incidents.vector: Hacked the FBI's recruitment website and dozens of other victims, then used a dedicated extortion site ("Shinywire") to pressure organizations into paying ransoms by threatening to publish stolen data.
incidents.impact: FBI personnel records, including medical/psychological files, Social Security numbers and home addresses, were stolen and threatened for release; the group has extorted more than $70 million from victims this year. U.S. authorities have arrested or detained several alleged members and facilitators, including a ransomware-negotiation-firm executive.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, government and manufacturing running unpatched PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Exploited an authentication-bypass vulnerability in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2026-0257) to establish VPN access, then pivoted to vCenter/ESXi infrastructure to dump domain credentials directly from virtual disks before deploying ransomware.
incidents.impact: Multiple ransomware operators (tracked as Qilin, Inc, and groups using Settra ransomware) have used this technique against organizations across numerous industries since June 2026.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime operators and global shipping companies (CyberLogitec customers)
incidents.vector: Compromised maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec and pivoted from its network into more than 40 downstream port authority, maritime and shipping company customers.
incidents.impact: All victims were listed on the group's dark web leak site; payment deadlines have expired for the initial batch of victims.
